title: Polynomial division for a monomial order
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\geq1$, and $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. A monomial order $\prec$ is a total well-order on $\mathbf N^r$, with $0$ least, preserved by addition. Write $\operatorname{LM}_\prec(f)$ for the greatest exponent with nonzero coefficient when $f\ne0$, and set $\operatorname{LM}_\prec(0)=0$. For any index set $T$, any family of nonzero polynomials $b_t\in S$ indexed by $t\in T$, and any $f\in S$, there are a finitely supported family $q:T\to S$ and a polynomial $h\in S$ such that
$$f=\sum_{t\in T}q_t b_t+h,$$
$$\operatorname{LM}_\prec(b_tq_t)\preceq\operatorname{LM}_\prec(f)\quad(t\in T),$$
and no exponent in the support of $h$ is coordinatewise greater than or equal to $\operatorname{LM}_\prec(b_t)$ for any $t\in T$. The support is the set of exponents with nonzero coefficient. This includes $T=\varnothing$, with $h=f$.
